name: voro++
why: 3D Voronoi tessellation software for real geometry work; a library, but a genuinely interesting one.

brief.what_it_is: Voro++ is a C++ software library for computing three-dimensional Voronoi tessellations. It takes a set of particle positions and computes the Voronoi cell for each particle individually, returning per-cell properties such as volume, centroid, and number of faces. It is built as a static library made of several C++ classes, and a command-line utility is also provided that exposes most of its features.
brief.why_it_exists: The author built it for cell-based statistics on particle systems, where features of each Voronoi cell are used to analyze the system. The homepage also says the direct cell-by-cell construction was meant to handle special boundary conditions and walls.
brief.how_it_works: Rather than building the whole tessellation at once, the library constructs each particle's cell directly, one cell at a time. The homepage says it uses algorithms that tolerate numerical precision errors. The homepage does not describe the underlying data structures.

commands_seen.context: Compiles the static library, command-line utility, and examples after config.mk has been reviewed. Run from the top-level directory.

brief.install_notes: No external dependencies are required to compile and run. Build with GNU Make after reviewing config.mk for your system's compiler and install settings. Install to /usr/local by default, so you may need to add those directories to your environment variables to use the library. Gnuplot (2D/3D plotting) and POV-Ray (rendering) are optional helpers for looking at output. On Windows without a terminal, the author reports success building in Microsoft Visual C++ Express and Code::Blocks; Cygwin works for the make route.
brief.standout: Cell-by-cell construction, rather than a global tessellation, is the stated distinguishing feature, and it is aimed at per-particle statistics and wall or special boundary handling. The author also cites a radical tessellation for polydisperse packings, contributed by a collaborator, which is a less common feature.
brief.status: Quiet. The download page lists version 0.4.6, released 10/17/2013, and says the 0.4 series was a major overhaul. The homepage and download page show no newer release or commit dates. Development is through a Subversion repository on code.lbl.gov. The site says it is maintained by Chris Rycroft.
brief.caveats: The download page lists the last release as 2013, so it may be unmaintained, and I did not check the repository for recent commits. Build and install are GNU Make-based: Mac and Linux are supported, Windows needs Cygwin or a manual import into an IDE. The homepage calls it a library, but it also ships a command-line utility; the scout note mentioned only the library. The documentation page was not fetched, so I could not confirm the API or the utility's usage.

The direct cell-by-cell construction makes the library particularly well-suited to handling special boundary conditions and walls.
This project is free, open-source software, released through the Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory and the US Department of Energy.

judge.reason: An uncommon computational-geometry tool that builds 3D Voronoi cells individually, enabling particle statistics and unusual wall or boundary conditions.

entry.title: Voro++
entry.tldr: A C++ library that computes a 3D Voronoi cell around each particle one at a time, returning volume, centroid, and face count per cell.
entry.deeper_look:
Voro++ takes a set of particle positions in three dimensions and works out the Voronoi cell for each one: the region of space closer to that particle than to any other. For each cell it can report properties such as volume, centroid, and number of faces. It is built as a static library of C++ classes, and a command-line utility is included that exposes most of its features.

The unusual part is how it gets there. Most tools build the whole tessellation at once. Voro++ builds each particle's cell directly, on its own. In the project's words: "A distinguishing feature of the Voro++ library is that it carries out cell-based calculations, computing the Voronoi cell for each particle individually." The homepage says this makes it well suited to special boundary conditions and walls, and that its algorithms tolerate numerical precision errors.

The author built it for cell-based statistics on particle systems, where the shape and size of each cell says something about how the particles are packed. It also includes a radical tessellation, contributed by a collaborator, for packings of particles of different sizes. Behind it sits a broader idea: partitioning space by nearest neighbour turns up in physics, materials science, and graphics, and the per-cell numbers are a way to measure a structure rather than just draw it.

It comes from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and is maintained by Chris Rycroft. Gnuplot and POV-Ray are optional helpers for looking at the output.
entry.install:
brew install voro++
# Builds from source otherwise: review config.mk, then run make and sudo make install (defaults to /usr/local). No external dependencies. Gnuplot and POV-Ray are optional for viewing output.
entry.whats_unique: It builds each Voronoi cell directly rather than computing a global tessellation, which suits per-particle statistics and walls or unusual boundaries. It also offers a radical tessellation for polydisperse packings.
entry.caveats: The last listed release is 0.4.6 from October 2013, and the brief did not check the repository for newer activity; the brew formula lists no executables, so the command-line utility may not be installed by it.
